definitions.explanation: Relating to actual substance or practical effect rather than form or appearance.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}が{実質的|じっしつてき}な{リーダー|りーだー}だ。
examples.english: He is the de facto leader.

examples.japanese: {実質的|じっしつてき}な{効果|こうか}は{見|み}られなかった。
{給料|きゅうりょう}は{実質的|じっしつてき}に{減|へ}っている。
examples.notes: Uses adverbial form 実質的に

notes:
FORMS:
・Adverbial: {実質的|じっしつてき}に (substantially, effectively)
・Noun: {実質|じっしつ} (substance, essence)

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{実質的|じっしつてき}な{効果|こうか}/{意味|いみ} (substantial effect/meaning)
・{実質的|じっしつてき}に{同|おな}じ (essentially the same)
・{実質的|じっしつてき}な{支配|しはい} (de facto control)

USAGE: Emphasizes actual substance over nominal or superficial aspects. Often used to describe what is true in practice, even if not officially recognized.

SIMILAR WORDS:
・{本質的|ほんしつてき}: Essential, fundamental (about inherent nature)
・{実質的|じっしつてき}: Substantial, practical (about actual effect)
